page.empty: No repositories or images scanned yet. Run a code or image scan to get started.
page.asset_placeholder: Search for a repository or image…
page.current_hint: scans and PRs combined, fixed items shown separately
page.removed: GitHub has had no access to this repository since {{date}} (it was deleted or removed from the App). If access doesn't come back, its findings, triage and linked tickets are deleted after 24 hours.

state.help: Combines full scans and PR reviews and keeps itself up to date: anything that stops showing up is marked fixed, and anything that comes back is reopened.

pr.scope: Only what this PR introduces shows up here.
pr.scope_preexisting_one: Only what this PR introduces shows up here; {{count}} finding in the code it touches already existed on the main branch and isn't counted.
pr.scope_preexisting_other: Only what this PR introduces shows up here; {{count}} findings in the code it touches already existed on the main branch and aren't counted.
pr.no_baseline: The main branch hadn't been scanned yet, so everything on changed lines counts.

scan.agreement_one: {{count}} advisory confirmed by both Trivy and Grype
scan.agreement_other: {{count}} advisories confirmed by both Trivy and Grype

empty.title: No findings in what was scanned
empty.body: The rules and dependencies we cover raised nothing. Check the coverage below to see what was left out.

table.no_match_dismissed_one: Nothing matches these filters · {{count}} dismissed in triage (change the status filter to see it).
table.no_match_dismissed_other: Nothing matches these filters · {{count}} dismissed in triage (change the status filter to see them).

group.malicious_hint: Known malicious package (OpenSSF): remove it and rotate any secrets on the machines where it was installed

detail.dev_hint: doesn't reach production, but it runs on your machine and in CI
detail.epss: EPSS · probability of exploitation in the next 30 days
detail.related: same issue as <mono>{{rules}}</mono>, merged so it isn't counted twice

lifecycle.label: Lifecycle:
lifecycle.excluded: Excluded: it's in a path an admin excluded. It doesn't count as open or block PRs.
lifecycle.excluded_pattern: Excluded: it's in a path an admin excluded ({{pattern}}). It doesn't count as open or block PRs.

sla_policy.title: Due dates:
sla_policy.scope: They apply to every repository, counted from first detection. The clock runs on open and in-progress findings; fixed findings and approved exceptions never come due.
sla_policy.admin_only: Only an admin can change them.
sla_policy.help: They apply to every repository, the Overview and reports. Leave a field empty so that severity never comes due. Defaults: 7, 30, 90 and 180 days.
sla_policy.invalid: Each due date is a whole number of days from 1 to 3650, or empty to leave it unset.

exclusions.title: Excluded paths
exclusions.active_help: Anything under these paths doesn't count as open or block PRs; you'll find it under Excluded.
exclusions.empty_help: For intentionally vulnerable samples, tests or generated code.
exclusions.admin_only: Only an admin can change them.
exclusions.patterns_help: One path per line, relative to the root: fixtures, docs/*.md, **/testdata. A folder excludes everything in it; “*” doesn't cross folders and “**” does.
exclusions.reason_placeholder: Why (kept in the history), e.g. “Intentionally vulnerable samples for testing the rules”
exclusions.saved: Saved. It also applies to upcoming scans and PR reviews.

description.open: It counts as pending again in the panel, tickets and SARIF.
description.in_progress: Someone is working on the fix. It still counts as pending.
description.false_positive: It stops counting as pending in this and future scans of the repository. The history records your user and the reason.
description.accepted: You take on the risk for a limited time: it stops counting as pending until the expiry date, then reopens on its own.
description.fixed: Marks it fixed without waiting for the next scan. Explain how it was fixed (PR, patch, deploy) so it's in the history. If the next scan finds it again, it reopens on its own.

placeholder.false_positive: e.g. The HTML comes from a static template and is sanitized with DOMPurify
placeholder.accepted: e.g. Not exposed to the internet; will be fixed in the Q4 migration
placeholder.fixed: e.g. Token revoked in Auth0 and removed from the README in PR #5

fix.title: How to fix it
fix.adapt: The example shows the pattern and its fix; adapt it to your code.

verify.running: Verifying: the scan is queued or running…
verify.fixed: Fixed ✓ · no longer found in the scan
verify.fixed_at: Fixed ✓ · no longer found in the scan from {{date}}
verify.present_at: Still present in the scan from {{date}}
verify.inconclusive: The scan was incomplete (an engine didn't run), so it proves nothing. Try again.
verify.failed: The verification scan failed. Try again.
verify.prompt: Already fixed it? Reverify: we scan the repository or image again and tell you whether it's still there.
verify.demo: Demo data: rescan it with “make demo”.
verify.open_pr: It comes from an open pull request, so it's verified on every push to the PR.

audit.mapping_note: The mapping to each control is indicative.
audit.title: Audit evidence report
audit.description: A concise PDF with scope, method, findings and their status, approved exceptions and sign-offs. Everything is optional: leave it as is to use the defaults.
audit.portfolio_scope: Every scanned repository in the organization, its coverage against GitHub (which ones lack a complete scan), open critical and high findings, and exceptions, in one document.
audit.exceptions: Include exceptions and decisions (accepted risks and false positives with their reason)
audit.disclaimer: This is technical evidence for the auditor, not an audit opinion or a certification. Review and sign it before you hand it over.
